This satisfies the wrong_target endpoint contract functionally (all three substates can reach PoweredOff), but it introduces a genuine cross-wrapper behavioral gap: NL2-ENDPOINT-2 requires the system to transition from Operate to PoweredOff on keyOff, yet the actual realized path is guarded by an SMT-unresolved (solver_status=not_run) boolean condition rather than an unconditional consequence of keyOff, meaning the required transition's exact guard/effect semantics cannot be certified sound by the frozen registry - this remains a precise but predicate-null W1 observation rather than a certified pass. No forbidden-scope entry, no dead-end/frontier faults, and no missing owner-entry across scopes were found. The guard_disjointness contract for Operate substate alternatives (accelerating/braking/stopping) is examined behaviorally: each substate transition is triggered by a distinct declared event (Accelerate_Signal, Brake_Signal, Stop_Signal) with no shared source-and-condition ambiguity, so alternatives remain operationally distinguishable and that contract is satisfied, omitted from candidates. The one behaviorally consequential defect is that Operate's keyOff exit is implemented as three separate per-substate transitions to [*] that set a shared route variable R45RouteToken=7, which is then consumed by a single guarded Operate->PoweredOff transition conditioned on R45RouteToken==7. This satisfies the wrong_target endpoint contract functionally (all three substates can reach PoweredOff), but it introduces a genuine cross-wrapper behavioral gap: NL2-ENDPOINT-2 requires the system to transition from Operate to PoweredOff on keyOff, yet the actual realized path is guarded by an SMT-unresolved (solver_status=not_run) boolean condition rather than an unconditional consequence of keyOff, meaning the required transition's exact guard/effect semantics cannot be certified sound by the frozen registry - this remains a precise but predicate-null W1 observation rather than a certified pass. No termination-state re-entry issue arises since PoweredOff can only be exited via 'start' (back into Operate) or 'end' (to final); this is intended power-cycling and not an unstable termination violation, so NL2-ENDPOINT-2's termination-adjacent risk is not separately flagged as termination since PoweredOff is not marked termination_state by contract. No forbidden-scope entry, no dead-end/frontier faults, and no missing owner-entry across scopes were found. The guard_disjointness contract for Operate substate alternatives (accelerating/braking/stopping) is examined behaviorally: each substate transition is triggered by a distinct declared event (Accelerate_Signal, Brake_Signal, Stop_Signal) with no shared source-and-condition ambiguity, so alternatives remain operationally distinguishable and that contract is satisfied, omitted from candidates. All containment, cardinality-free declaration, and endpoint contracts are satisfied by the reachable inventory and are omitted.

decisions.basis: exact_source_inventory tr_0001, inspection_equivalent_facts transition:line:23, NL-CONTRACT-NL1-INITENTRY-1 requirement quote, verify_facts initial-entry proof for transition:line:23
decisions.reason: The exact source inventory (tr_0001) and closed-model transition:line:23 both show the root initial edge [*] -> PoweredOff, not [*] -> Operate; Operate is only reached later via a separate start-signal transition from PoweredOff. NL1's literal text ('Once the device is powered on, the system enters the Operate state') supports reading this as a root-owned default-entry obligation that is violated by the PoweredOff target. A competent alternative reading survives: NL2 independently frames PoweredOff as the true power-off/initial condition and Operate as reached one signal-step later, so the compressed NL1 clause could be a narrative gloss over the two-step PoweredOff->Operate(start) flow rather than a literal single root-initial-edge requirement. Because both readings are compatible with the same exact transition facts and neither is excluded by an explicit contract clause resolving the ambiguity, this remains an undercutting defeater rather than a full rebuttal.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL1 requires that the root/device-owned initial pseudostate edge, fired upon power-on, must directly enter the Operate state.

decisions.basis: fcstm_model.text lines 17-19 and 22, inspection_equivalent_facts transition:line:17/18/19/22, smt_facts guard:transition:line:22, NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED requirement quote, working_contract macro-pattern hint
decisions.reason: The closed model facts (fcstm_model lines 17-19, 22) show keyOff is consumed inside Operate's substates, setting effect R45RouteToken=7, while the actual Operate->PoweredOff composite edge (transition:line:22) carries guard R45RouteToken==7 with an empty trigger list rather than a direct keyOff trigger; smt_facts mark the guard formula solver_status=not_run. NL2's literal text states the system is 'turned off with the keyOff signal', which supports a direct, unconditional keyOff-triggered exit reading that this indirect guarded-token construct does not literally satisfy. A competent alternative reading survives: the working_contract's identification of this as a protected compiler-owned macro construct for composite-exit routing suggests the keyOff-effect-then-guarded-exit pattern may be an authorized generated-code lowering of UML composite-exit semantics rather than an authored deviation. However, no exact supplied fact confirms the macro closes end-to-end equivalently for every Operate substate and every path, and the solver status is not_run, so this alternative is a genuinely compatible but unconfirmed reading rather than a fact-established rebuttal, making it an undercutting defeater.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL2 requires that the keyOff signal alone causes the system to leave Operate and enter PoweredOff, without an additional unstated guard condition.

issues.requirement_quote: and turned off with the `keyOff` signal

issues.observed: In the closed FCSTM, keyOff fires three separate substate-local transitions (Idle->[*], AcceleratingOrCruising->[*], Braking->[*] at lines 17/18/19) that only set R45RouteToken=7; the actual Operate->PoweredOff transition (line 22) is a second, distinct transition guarded by R45RouteToken==7 and is not itself triggered by keyOff (its triggers list is empty). The SMT formula for this guard has solver_status=not_run, so the exact condition under which Operate transitions to PoweredOff is not certified; the keyOff-to-PoweredOff behavioral consequence depends on an unverified two-step relay rather than one direct guarded/triggered edge.
issues.reason: The NL obligation is a direct semantic endpoint pair (Operate -> PoweredOff) triggered by keyOff; the closed model's realization splits this into a triggered variable-setting step and a separately guarded, untriggered consumption step whose guard formula is not solver-verified, which is a distinct behavioral-consequence fact from a certified direct endpoint and must remain visible even though the composite path likely satisfies the intent.
issues.requirement_quote: and turned off with the `keyOff` signal
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Functionally, from every reachable Operate substate, firing keyOff followed immediately by the resulting guard evaluation is deterministic (R45RouteToken is set to exactly 7 and immediately consumed with no intervening event), so the composite behavior is operationally equivalent to a direct Operate--keyOff-->PoweredOff transition and the contract's exact endpoint pair (Operate, PoweredOff) is realized through this protected macro relay.
